name: Shah Muhammad Sagir
seoTitle: Shah Muhammad Sagir: Poet of Yusuf-Zulekha in Bengal
seoDescription: Shah Muhammad Sagir was a late-fourteenth- or early-fifteenth-century Bengali poet whose Yusuf-Zulekha brought Perso-Arabic literary themes into Bengali verse.
role: Court poet and pioneer of Bengali Muslim literature
contribution: Shah Muhammad Sagir wrote Yusuf-Zulekha, a Bengali narrative poem based on the Qur'anic story of Joseph and Zulekha. Its praise of Sultan Ghiyasuddin Azam Shah suggests that Sagir was probably a court poet and composed the work under the Sultan's patronage or request.
context: The late-fourteenth- and early-fifteenth-century literary world of the Bengal Sultanate, when Persian and Arabic narrative and devotional traditions were being adapted for Bengali-speaking audiences.
impact: Sagir is often regarded as the first Bengali writer to bring Perso-Arabic literary themes into Bengali. Yusuf-Zulekha combines religious teaching with human love, uses payar and tripadi metres, and includes references to musical modes that suggest parts of the poem were designed for singing.
